text:
carmen: quick ping — onboarding report: a few folks hit 401s after yesterday's rotation when running the sampleapp locally.

ben: are they pulling keys from env? which var name did they use?

carmen: yes, env. they copied snippets from older internal docs that use REDWOOD_KEY. our README uses REDWOOD_API_KEY, but we still have scattered REDWOOD_TOKEN examples.

jules: classic. SDK parity gap. we should standardize accepted names across languages and log a deprecation notice for legacy names.

ben: agree. minimal plan: (1) SDKs accept REDWOOD_API_KEY, then REDWOOD_KEY, then REDWOOD_TOKEN; (2) emit a one-line deprecation warning when KEY or TOKEN are used; (3) update sampleapp READMEs.

carmen: also support asked for better troubleshooting text. 401 just says "unauthorized" and customers get stuck. can SDKs expand the message? e.g. "401 Unauthorized — possible causes: key rotated, key is project-scoped, or env var mismatch. Run `rw auth env` to print export lines."

jules: yea. small change in error mapper is low-risk. also adding server-side tag for rotation-suspected when key matches legacy-prefix will help product/support find impacted runs.

ben: i'll open PRs for js + py SDKs to normalize env lookup and the richer 401. sam — can you patch sampleapp and README?

carmen: one UX idea: CLI helper `rw auth env` (or `rw auth export`) that prints shell-friendly export commands so users can quickly rehydrate their local session after rotation. saves a ton of hand-holding.

jules: I'll prototype the CLI helper. simple output: `# bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=rw_...` and optionally a note about org vs project scope.

ops-bot: rotation-audit: rotated by ops@customercorp at 2025-05-06T12:04:22Z; old_prefix=rw_a12b; new_prefix=rw_x98y; clients_impacted=4

carmen: thanks all — please link PRs in the support ticket and add the troubleshooting blurb to the onboarding checklist. small coordinated changes should fix the bulk of these immediate onboarding failures. :thumbsup:
